sections.title: P15-Q1 — PHP/Composer/Laravel rename boundaries
sections.text:
Status: `success`

Query:

> Using only current official PHP, Composer, and Laravel documentation, what must a pre-1.0 PHP library check when renaming public classes/interfaces, promoted public properties, a Laravel Artisan command class while keeping its command signature, a Composer package name, and a class FQCN that might be stored in a database? Explain limits of class_alias and Composer replace. Give direct primary-source links and separate sourced facts from practical recommendations.

sections.title: Perplexity response
sections.text:
A pre-1.0 version does not make these changes mechanically safe: PHP, Composer,
Laravel, databases, serialized payloads, and downstream user code all have separate
identity surfaces. Before renaming, inventory every surface where the old identifier
is resolved, invoked, reflected on, persisted, or installed; then decide whether to
preserve it with a compatibility layer or deliberately break it.

For public classes and interfaces the response names direct imports, `::class`
strings, reflection/container/configuration maps, interface implementations,
Composer PSR-4 paths and optimized autoload as separate surfaces. For promoted public
properties it calls out both named constructor arguments and direct property access;
PHP has no property equivalent of `class_alias()`.

For Laravel commands the command signature owns the CLI name, arguments and options,
while discovery or explicit `withCommands([ClassName::class])` may still reference the
class FQCN. Calls by signature can survive a class rename; calls by old class name do
not. The response recommends checking `artisan list`, `artisan help` and programmatic
invocation after the move.

For Composer package renames, `replace` is dependency-solver metadata. It does not
relocate namespaces, provide old FQCNs, register Laravel commands, migrate data or
rewrite consumer source. Version bounds matter; Composer's documented subpackage
pattern uses `self.version` rather than claiming arbitrary compatibility.

`class_alias()` aliases runtime class identity only. It does not alias a property,
constructor argument, method, enum case, constant, configuration key, Composer package
or database value. The alias must execute before the old name is resolved, and it
cannot translate a changed constructor, public property or behavior. If an FQCN is
stored in a database, an alias may keep reads alive temporarily but does not migrate
the stored value.

Practical recommendations in the response are explicitly non-normative: inventory
all string/persisted surfaces, test the normal Composer autoloader, preserve the
Artisan signature, use stable application-owned keys instead of persisted FQCNs, and
test real downstream dependency graphs for a package rename. CoreX adopts the
inventory and negative-test shape, not the suggested additive compatibility release:
the local 1.0 boundary deliberately performs clean renames under G-API and leaves no
deprecated aliases unless an actual external consumer is demonstrated.

Primary links returned:

- https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.class-alias.php
- https://getcomposer.org/doc/04-schema.md#replace
- https://laravel.com/docs/12.x/artisan
- https://laravel.com/docs/master/artisan

Direct verification after the MCP response:

- Composer schema body SHA256:
  `a6d258f7feb334e943a8bb34f61a2d2927fbd22f5acb0e15f80f5620aa589303`;
  `replace` and `self.version` wording observed.
- Laravel 13 `artisan.md` body SHA256:
  `30086e176acdd8a8575767b0d0bae55380a883d883df96d6fa89da4eb2cdce20`;
  default discovery, `withCommands` class registration and `Artisan::call` observed.
- PHP manual was retrieved once and identified `class_alias` as creating a class
  alias; a later full-body retry failed DNS resolution, so no full-body digest is
  claimed.

The generic web connector separately failed with `connection failed`; it is not
counted as evidence.
